name.text: Finding equations, range, domain, and the graph of exponential function

questiontext.text:
Consider the following questions:

Note: To enter intervals of real line, you should write the relevant text in the table below.

Intervals Input Syntax
\( [a,b] \) cc(a,b)
\( (a,b) \) oo(a,b)
\( [a,b) \) co(a,b)
\( (a,b] \) oc(a,b)
\( (a, \infty) \) oo(a,inf)
\( (-\infty, b] \) oc(-inf,b)
\( (-\infty, \infty) \) oo(-inf,inf)

a) Write an equation that defines the exponential function with base \(a> 0\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

b) What is the domain of the function in \((a)\)?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

c) If \(a \neq 1,\) what is the range of the function in \((a)\)?

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

[[feedback:prt3]]

d) Drag slidders \(a\) to graph the exponetial function in part a when:

i. \(a >1\)

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="500px" input-ref-ansa='ansaRef']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-8, 8, 8, -8], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation:true }); var sliderA = board.create('slider', [[-6, 3], [-3, 3], [0, {#a1#}, 3]],{name:'a', snapWidth: 0.1}); // Function to plot the exponential curve (a > 1) function plotExponentialGreaterThanOne(a) { var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return a.Value() **x ; }]); return curve; } // Plotting the exponential curve for a > 1 var curve = plotExponentialGreaterThanOne(sliderA); // Label for slider board.create('text', [-4, 9, function() { return 'a = ' + sliderA.Value(); }]); stack_jxg.bind_slider(ansaRef,sliderA); board.update(); [[/jsxgraph]]

[[input:ansa]] [[validation:ansa]] [[feedback:prta]]

ii. \(a =1\)

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="500px" input-ref-ans5='ans5Ref']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-8, 8, 8, -8], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation:true }); // Define slider for a var sliderA = board.create('slider', [[-6, 3], [-3, 3], [0, {#b1#}, 3]],{name:'a', snapWidth: 0.1}); // Function to plot the exponential curve (a = 1) function plotExponentialEqualsOne(a) { var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return a.Value() **x ; }]); return curve; } // Plotting the exponential curve for a = 1 var curve = plotExponentialEqualsOne(sliderA); stack_jxg.bind_slider(ans5Ref,sliderA); board.update(); [[/jsxgraph]]

[[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]][[feedback:prt5]]

iii. \(0 < a <1\)

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="500px" input-ref-ans6='ans6Ref']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox:[-8, 8, 8, -8], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation:true }); // Define slider for a var sliderA = board.create('slider', [[-6, 3], [-3, 3], [0, {#a1#}, 3]],{name:'a', snapWidth: 0.1}); // Function to plot the exponential curve (0 < a < 1) function plotExponentialBetweenZeroAndOne(a) { var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return a.Value() **x ; }]); return curve; } // Plotting the exponential curve for 0 < a < 1 var curve = plotExponentialBetweenZeroAndOne(sliderA); stack_jxg.bind_slider(ans6Ref, sliderA); board.update(); [[/jsxgraph]]

[[input:ans6]] [[validation:ans6]][[feedback:prt6]]
